title: PHP post-login redirect and remember-me
context: Finishes a login: optionally sets a remember-me cookie and redirects to ?return=. Only same-site relative paths are allowed (a single leading "/" followed by a non-slash, non-backslash character); anything else goes to /dashboard. The remember-me cookie must be Secure and HttpOnly, and only a SHA-256 hash of the token may be stored in the database.
code: $pdo->prepare('UPDATE users SET last_login_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?')->execute([$userId]);

expected.why: the raw token is stored in token_hash, so a database leak hands out working remember-me cookies; store hash('sha256', $token)
the cookie is readable from JavaScript, so any XSS can steal the long-lived login token
"//evil.example" and "/\evil.example" start with "/" but are protocol-relative URLs, so this is an open redirect
